title: Integration on the surreals: a conjecture of Conway, Kruskal and Norton
note: Two-sided result on integration over $\mathbf{No}$. Positive: defines a robust algebraic integral for semi-algebraic, analytic, and Écalle–Borel transserial functions by routing through Hardy-field germs and the surreal–transseries correspondence. Negative: proves set-theoretic obstructions ruling out a translation-invariant integration operator on the full ring $C(\mathbf{No})$ of continuous surreal functions. Motivates the audit-style 'what survives' framing of \ref{rem:analytic-obstructions}: QOU never needs a measure on $C(\mathbf{No})$ — only the algebraic transfer of a small set of field-polymorphic constructions, all of which lift unchanged (\ref{rem:algebraic-core-survives}).
